title: Veneers vs crowns vs Invisalign: what actually fixes your front teeth?
seoTitle: Veneers vs Crowns vs Invisalign: Which Fixes Your Front Teeth?
description: Veneers, crowns or Invisalign for front teeth, decided problem by problem: how much tooth each removes, how long each takes, what each costs in Miami, when a crown is honest.
author: Dr. Marta Puentes Marrero, DMD
imageAlt: Dentist comparing a clear aligner and a dental model with a patient
answer: It depends on the problem, not the product. **Stains, chips, small gaps and mild crowding**: porcelain veneers, with 0.3 to 0.7 mm of enamel removed, done in one week. **A broken, root-canalled or heavily filled tooth**: a crown, which removes most of the tooth but is the honest choice. **Moderate crowding or a bite that does not meet**: Invisalign first, over months, then veneers only where still needed. At Xiluet Smiles, 20 veneers cost **$6,000** and Invisalign **$4,000**.

sections.h2: Start with the problem, not the product

blocks.p: Veneers, crowns and aligners do three different jobs. A veneer changes the color, shape and length of the front of a tooth. A crown rebuilds a whole tooth that cannot hold itself together. Invisalign moves teeth, roots included, but does not change their color or shape. Most front-teeth problems point clearly to one of them. This is how we sort them at Visit 1.

list: **Stains that whitening cannot lift** (tetracycline, fluorosis, a dark root-canalled tooth): veneers. A crown removes far too much tooth for a color problem.
**Chipped or worn edges**: veneers. A crown only if the tooth is cracked through or has lost most of its structure.
**Gaps**: veneers in one week, or aligners over months if you would rather keep every bit of enamel and have the time.
**Mild crowding or one rotated tooth**: veneers, or aligners if you prefer. Both work; the difference is time and whether you also want a color or shape change.

**Moderate to severe crowding, an overbite or a crossbite**: aligners first. Veneers alone would need heavy preparation on the teeth that stick out to fake a straight line, and that is where damage happens.
**A broken, root-canalled or heavily filled tooth**: a crown. There is not enough enamel left to bond a veneer to.
**A missing tooth**: none of the three. An implant or a bridge, planned together with whatever the neighbours need.

blocks.p: Many smiles need a mix. Two crowns on broken teeth, eight veneers beside them, and the rest left alone is a normal plan. The point is to pick per tooth, not to pick one product and apply it to everything.

sections.h2: How much tooth each one removes

blocks.p: This is the question most patients wish they had asked. A porcelain veneer takes 0.3 to 0.7 mm from the front surface of the tooth, and a well-planned one stays inside the enamel; at 0.3 mm, sometimes nothing is removed at all. A crown is prepared on every surface, front, back, sides and biting edge, so that the cap can wrap the tooth. Cosmetic dentists who warn about "Turkey teeth" put crown preparation at roughly [60 to 70 percent of the visible tooth](https://www.theperfectsmile.co.uk/news/why-you-should-avoid-turkey-teeth-like-the-plague), against a thin layer for a veneer. Invisalign removes nothing, apart from an occasional polish of a fraction of a millimetre between crowded teeth to make room.

Why enamel matters: in a [15-year study of 672 veneers](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jerd.70016), veneers bonded to enamel survived 96.7% of the time against 93.9% when more than 30% of the bonded surface was dentin, and dentin exposure raised the odds of failure 3.5 times. Enamel is the best bonding surface there is, and it does not grow back. That is the whole argument for choosing the least invasive option that solves your problem.

It is also why crowns sold as veneers are a problem. A British Dental Association survey found that [86% of UK dentists had treated complications](https://www.bda.org/media-centre/uk-dentists-picking-up-the-pieces-from-dental-tourism-boom/) from dental work done abroad, and 87% of them named crowns. Twenty crowns on twenty healthy teeth is not a smile design. It is twenty teeth that will need a crown for the rest of your life.

sections.h2: When a crown is the honest answer

blocks.p: None of this means crowns are bad. A crown is the right restoration for a tooth that needs holding together: a tooth that has broken, one with a large old filling and thin walls, a root-canalled tooth that has become brittle, or a tooth worn so far down that the bite height has to be rebuilt. On those teeth a veneer has nothing to bond to and would fail; a crown wraps the remaining structure and protects it. Porcelain and zirconia crowns typically last 10 to 30 years with good care.

At Xiluet, a porcelain crown is $500 when done with your smile design (the list price is $1,000), and the [Complete Restoration package](/complete-restoration-miami) covers 20 crowns, bridges or veneers for $7,000, delivered in 5 business days with a 5-year written warranty. Crowns and bridges are often classed as major restorative work by insurers and may be covered 50 to 80 percent depending on your plan; we give you the codes for your claim. Veneers are classed as cosmetic and almost never covered.

The honest version is simple: a crown on a tooth that needs one, matched in color and shape to the veneers beside it, in the same lab, by the same ceramist. The dishonest version is a crown on a healthy tooth because it is faster to prepare or because the clinic calls everything a veneer.

Veneers can straighten the look of mildly crowded or rotated teeth in a week, and for many patients that is the right call. The line is crossed when a tooth sits clearly in front of its neighbours, when teeth overlap, or when the upper and lower teeth do not meet properly. Making those teeth look straight with porcelain means grinding the prominent ones back into line, often through the enamel and into dentin, which is exactly the situation the survival data warns about. Dentists who compare the two options give the same rule: [mask mild misalignment with veneers, align moderate crowding first](https://www.alldentals.com/blog/fixing-crooked-teeth-the-difference-between-invisalign-and-veneers/).

Aligning first takes months rather than days and needs a retainer afterwards to hold the result. The payoff is that once the teeth sit where they should, you usually need fewer veneers, or none, and whatever veneers you do need are prepared minimally because nothing has to be forced into line. Invisalign is on our [price list](/veneers-cost-miami) at $4,000 and a retainer at $400. If aligners should come first, we tell you in the written estimate before you book anything.

The one thing aligners cannot do is change color, shape or length. If your teeth are straight but short, dark or chipped, aligners are the wrong tool. And if they are crooked but you also want them whiter and longer, the sequence is align, then veneer.

blocks.p: The veneer survival figure comes from a [pooled analysis of about 6,500 veneers](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7961608/). Failures cluster in the first two years and are mostly fractures or debonds, which is one reason a written multi-year warranty is worth asking for. Most Miami practices we found in October 2026 offered none or one year.

blocks.quote: If I can keep your enamel, I will. A crown is for a tooth that needs holding together, not for a tooth that needs a new color.

sections.h2: Five questions to ask any dentist

steps: **Which teeth get which treatment, and why?** The answer should be per tooth, not "a full set".
**How much tooth comes off each one, in millimetres?** Anything close to a millimetre on every surface is a crown, whatever it is called.
**Does the restoration cover the back of the tooth?** If yes, it is a crown.
**Would aligning first mean fewer veneers or less preparation?** A good answer admits when the answer is yes.
**Can I see the design in my mouth before anything is prepared, and can I have the price and warranty in writing?** If either answer is no, keep looking.

faq.a: Mild crowding and a single rotated tooth, yes, in one week. Moderate or severe crowding, no. Those teeth should be aligned first, otherwise the prominent ones have to be ground back into line, which is where veneers damage teeth.

faq.q: Are crowns better than veneers for front teeth?
faq.a: Only when the tooth is broken, root-canalled or heavily filled. On a healthy tooth a crown removes enamel you cannot get back, for no benefit over a veneer.

faq.q: Can I get veneers after Invisalign?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a common sequence. Once the teeth are in position you usually need fewer veneers, and the preparation is minimal because nothing has to be forced straight. Wear your retainer; veneers do not hold teeth in place.

faq.q: How do I know if I am being sold crowns as veneers?
faq.a: Ask how much tooth will be removed, in millimetres, and whether the restoration covers the back of the tooth. A veneer covers the front and takes 0.3 to 0.7 mm. A crown wraps every surface. Get the answer in writing before you pay a deposit.

faq.q: Does insurance cover crowns but not veneers?
faq.a: Often, yes. Crowns are usually classed as major restorative work and may be covered 50 to 80 percent depending on your plan; we give you the codes. Veneers are classed as cosmetic and almost never covered. Check your plan for orthodontic benefits before starting Invisalign.

faq.q: How much does Invisalign cost at Xiluet Smiles?
faq.a: $4,000, with a retainer at $400 to hold the result. Your final fee is confirmed in writing after a doctor's evaluation.
